strengths: The paper is well-motivated and clearly structured, tackling two critical issues in compositional video generation (semantic leakage during text encoding and rigid/inaccurate spatial binding during denoising) through a coherent dual-phase design.

The proposed method is entirely training-free and model-agnostic, showing seamless integration and consistent gains across both DiT (CogVideoX-2B) and U-Net (VideoCrafter2) backbones with modest inference latency overhead (only 16-21%).

The Dynamic Layout Fusion Attention (DLFA) smartly bridges the gap between rigid LLM-generated bounding boxes and real subject geometries by dynamically deriving model-perceived masks from cross-modal attention maps with an adaptive threshold.

Extensive quantitative evaluations on T2V-CompBench and VBench, alongside meaningful qualitative visualizations and thorough ablation studies (isolating SAD, DLFA, 3D Region Attention, and Word Swapping), convincingly validate the contribution.
weaknesses: The pipeline relies on an external LLM (ChatGLM-4) to generate the initial bounding box priors and subject decomposition, making the system dependent on the spatial reasoning capabilities and consistency of the upstream language model.

The paper lacks a user study or human perceptual evaluation, which is important for compositional video generation to assess whether localized noise sampling and masked attention introduce boundary artifacts, blending seams, or temporal flicker.

Evaluation is primarily focused on relatively lightweight models (CogVideoX-2B and VideoCrafter2); demonstrating applicability on state-of-the-art larger models (e.g., CogVideoX-5B or HunyuanVideo) would further reinforce the method's generalizability.

The interaction between highly overlapping or interacting subjects (e.g., severe occlusions where bounding boxes heavily intersect) is not thoroughly analyzed in terms of mask fusion behavior in DLFA.

strengths: Principled dual-phase design: The paper cleanly decomposes compositional text-to-video generation into two complementary stages—resolving semantic confusion during prompt encoding via Semantic Anchor Disambiguation (SAD) and enforcing fine-grained spatio-temporal binding during sampling via Dynamic Layout Fusion Attention (DLFA).

Training-free and model-agnostic: MagicComp requires no parameter fine-tuning, LoRA training, or expensive test-time optimization loops. It seamlessly integrates into both modern DiT architectures (CogVideoX) and UNet-based pipelines (VideoCrafter2) with modest inference overhead (~16-21%).

Comprehensive empirical validation: Evaluated across standard compositional benchmarks (T2V-CompBench and VBench) covering attribute binding, spatial relations, motion, interaction, and numeracy. MagicComp yields significant quantitative gains over base models and outperforms or remains highly competitive against specialized compositional baselines.

Well-structured ablation studies: The ablations convincingly demonstrate the individual and combined efficacy of SAD and DLFA, while comparing favorably against alternative strategies such as Word Swap and 3D Region Attention.
weaknesses: Reliance and sensitivity to the LLM prior: The framework relies on an upstream LLM (ChatGLM-4) to extract subject entities and produce coarse spatiotemporal bounding boxes. The manuscript lacks an analysis of sensitivity or failure cases stemming from LLM hallucination, inaccurate bounding box planning, or missing entities in complex scenarios.

Mask fusion formulation: In Equation (7), the fused mask is computed as $L^{\text{fuse}} = L^{\text{prior}} \cup L^{\text{adapt}}$. Because the union operation strictly expands or retains the coarse bounding box $L^{\text{prior}}$, background noise enclosed within the original box cannot be pruned away by $L^{\text{adapt}}$, potentially limiting how fine-grained the refined mask can actually be.

Notational ambiguity in time attenuation: In Section 3.2, the paper specifies $\omega(t) = 1 - t/T$ with the rationale that early denoising requires stronger disambiguation semantics than late stages. In standard diffusion notation, $t=T$ corresponds to the initial high-noise step and $t=0$ to the clean output, which would yield $\omega(T) = 0$ (i.e., vanishing guidance at the start). Clarifying whether $t$ indexes the reverse sampling step index or the diffusion noise level is necessary.

Backbone scale and evaluation: Experiments are focused on CogVideoX-2B and VideoCrafter2. Validating the technique on larger contemporary backbones (e.g., CogVideoX-5B or HunyuanVideo) and supplementing automated T2V-CompBench metrics with a user study would significantly strengthen the empirical claims.

strengths: Training-free and model-agnostic pipeline: MagicComp operates without parameter updates, LoRA tuning, or test-time backpropagation, making it readily applicable to both DiT-based (CogVideoX-2B) and UNet-based (VideoCrafter2) video diffusion models with modest inference time overhead (16%–21%).

Coherent dual-phase formulation: Decomposing the compositional generation challenge into semantic disambiguation at the text condition stage (SAD) and spatial-attribute binding during denoising (DLFA) is a logical and structured approach.

Solid quantitative results on established benchmarks: Demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple categories on T2V-CompBench (e.g., Consist-attr, Spatial, Interaction) and VBench over the baseline models and several competitive compositional methods.

Comprehensive modular ablations: The paper provides clear ablations isolating the benefits of SAD and DLFA individually, and compares DLFA against standard 3D region attention and SAD against simple word swapping.
weaknesses: Conceptual flaw in layout mask refinement via union: In Section 3.3, DLFA derives an adaptive mask $L^{adapt}$ and sets $L^{fuse} = L^{prior} \cup L^{adapt}$, where $L^{prior}$ is a coarse 2D bounding box generated by an LLM. Because a set union operation can only expand or keep the mask size identical, it cannot eliminate background or non-object pixels already enclosed within the coarse bounding box. This directly conflicts with the stated motivation of refining coarse bounding boxes into tight, fine-grained object contours.

Contradiction in the timestep weighting formulation: Section 3.2 states that 'the early stages of denoising require clearer semantics... while the later stages... focus more on leveraging context', motivating $\omega(t) = 1 - t/T$. Under standard diffusion notation where $t=T$ corresponds to pure noise (the early stage) and $t=0$ corresponds to the clean video (the final stage), $\omega(t)$ evaluates to 0 at the start and 1 at the end, which directly contradicts the authors' textual justification.

Heavy reliance on external LLM layout quality without sensitivity analysis: DLFA critically depends on ChatGLM-4 to decompose prompts and generate valid spatiotemporal bounding boxes across keyframes. The paper lacks analysis regarding model sensitivity, error propagation, or failure cases when the LLM outputs incorrect, overlapping, or out-of-frame bounding boxes.

Notation inconsistencies: In Eq. (3), the perturbation term uses $\Delta_i$ instead of the previously defined $\Delta A_k$ / $\Delta A_i$. Additionally, the tensor broadcasting operation $\oplus$ between token embeddings and pooled directional vectors is not clearly defined for variable-length sequence representations.

Absence of human perceptual evaluation: Automated evaluation metrics on T2V-CompBench and VBench can be noisy, particularly for complex interaction, multi-object counts, and temporal consistency. A structured user study comparing visual realism, text alignment, and motion plausibility against strong baselines would be necessary to substantiate the qualitative claims.

strengths: Principled problem formulation: The paper clearly identifies and decouples two distinct failure modes in compositional text-to-video generation—subject omission/suppression at the conditioning level and relational misalignment at the spatial attention level—introducing the 'Present-and-Align' paradigm.

Technically sound and novel mechanisms: Subject-aware Condition Interpolation (SCI) provides an elegant semantic restoration mechanism based on subject saliency without corrupting contextual prompt semantics. Layout-forcing Attention Modulation (LAM) replaces rigid hard-masking and expensive latent optimization with soft, IoU-guided feedback modulation.

Extensive empirical validation: The framework is evaluated across diverse, contemporary foundation architectures, including DiT (Wan2.1, Wan2.2), MM-DiT (CogVideoX, FLUX), and U-Net (VideoCrafter2). Significant quantitative gains are achieved on T2V-CompBench (e.g., +15.71% on Wan2.1, +11.70% on Wan2.2) and T2I-CompBench.

Preservation of video quality and efficiency: Unlike test-time latent optimization methods (e.g., ViCo, LVD) that degrade baseline visual fidelity on VBench and increase runtime by 60–90%, Comp-Attn incurs only ~5% runtime overhead and maintains or slightly improves VBench quality scores.

Thorough ablations and robustness analysis: The authors provide detailed modular ablations (Table 5, 6, 7), interpolation hyperparameter comparisons (Table 8), and an analysis of LLM layout error rates and keyframe interpolation strategies (Table 9).
weaknesses: Dependency on external LLMs for layout generation: While GPT-4o-mini is efficient and cost-effective, the pipeline's spatial accuracy is bounded by the LLM's spatial reasoning and layout planning capabilities, which can still produce non-physical motion trajectories or size estimations in highly dynamic or complex scenes.

Lack of human evaluation: The evaluation relies exclusively on automated metrics (T2V-CompBench, VBench, T2I-CompBench). Given known perception and alignment biases in automated evaluation toolkits, a small-scale human preference study assessing compositional correctness and motion naturalness would strengthen the claims.

Simplification in temporal layout interpolation: Generating bounding boxes for 4 keyframes followed by linear interpolation assumes predominantly piecewise linear object trajectories, which may struggle with erratic, non-linear, or rapid 3D camera/object motions.

strengths: The paper addresses two fundamental and prevalent failure modes in compositional text-to-video (T2V) generation—subject omission and relational misalignment—via a well-motivated and coherent 'Present-and-Align' paradigm.

The proposed Subject-aware Condition Interpolation (SCI) provides an elegant, training-free way to restore suppressed subject semantics directly in the condition space using dynamic saliency estimation, avoiding invasive latent optimization.

Layout-forcing Attention Modulation (LAM) introduces an effective soft, IoU-guided modulation mechanism that adaptively aligns cross-attention maps with planned bounding boxes, overcoming the rigidity and visual artifact issues common to hard-masking approaches.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across diverse video architectures (DiT in Wan2.1/2.2, MM-DiT in CogVideoX, U-Net in VideoCrafter2) and image generation (FLUX) demonstrates substantial gains on T2V-CompBench (+11.7% to +29.8%) and VBench with minimal computational overhead (~5% latency increase).

Thorough ablations and diagnostic analyses (e.g., verifying the role of IoU-guidance, saliency-weighted interpolation vs. fixed ratios, and analyzing LLM keyframe planning error rates) provide solid support for the individual design choices.
weaknesses: The pipeline relies on an external closed-source LLM (GPT-4o-mini) for layout generation and parsing, introducing external API dependencies and potential failure points; the paper would benefit from evaluating whether open-source, locally runnable small language models can perform layout planning comparably.

The trajectory planning relies on 4 LLM-generated keyframes with linear interpolation for intermediate frames, which may struggle with complex, non-linear trajectories, fast rotational dynamics, or severe camera motion.
Deriving the adaptive-perception layout via mean-thresholded cross-attention maps (Eq. 5) can be noisy or unstable when dealing with heavily occluded, deformable, or transparent objects.

The decision to apply Comp-Attn only during the first 20% of denoising timesteps is justified conceptually, but a sensitivity analysis over this cutoff percentage across different base models is missing.

strengths: Principled and decoupled problem formulation: Decomposing compositional video generation into subject presence (handled at the textual condition level) and inter-subject relational alignment (handled at the cross-attention distribution level) is conceptually well-motivated and addresses key failure modes of existing layout-only or optimization-only methods.

Remarkable computational efficiency: Unlike test-time latent optimization techniques (e.g., LVD, ViCo) that require costly backpropagation and gradient calculation at each diffusion step (increasing latency by 60-90%), Comp-Attn achieves significant performance gains with only approximately 5% additional runtime overhead.

Comprehensive empirical validation across diverse backbones: The method is validated on multiple distinct architectures, including DiT (Wan2.1-14B, Wan2.2-A14B), MM-DiT (CogVideoX-5B, FLUX.1), and U-Net (VideoCrafter2) across T2V-CompBench, VBench, and T2I-CompBench, consistently outperforming training-free and several commercial baselines.

Well-structured ablation studies: The paper isolates the contributions of Subject-aware Condition Interpolation (SCI) and Layout-forcing Attention Modulation (LAM), demonstrates the necessity of dynamic IoU guidance over static gating, and validates semantic saliency estimation against fixed interpolation baselines.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on external LLM planning: The spatial and temporal alignment fundamentally depends on the bounding-box trajectory generated by an external LLM (GPT-4o-mini). While keyframe interpolation reduces errors, inaccurate or physically implausible LLM plans can misguide the dynamic attention bias.

Simplistic temporal trajectory modeling: Interpolating linearly across only 4 keyframes over 49 to 81 latent video frames is inherently restrictive. It assumes smooth, linear object trajectories and struggles to capture complex non-linear motion, erratic trajectories, or abrupt camera movements.

Lack of human evaluation: Given known noise and biases in automated VLM/CLIP-based compositional metrics (such as those in T2V-CompBench and VBench), the evaluation would be substantially strengthened by a rigorous blind user study assessing subject fidelity, spatial correctness, and temporal consistency.

Mathematical precision in attention modulation formulation: In Section 3.3, the dimensional broadcasting and formulation of Equations (6)–(10) (specifically how the scalar/vector terms $g^+_i$, $g^-_i$, and spatial layout mask $L_k$ operate over $N_{	ext{video}} 	imes N_{	ext{text}}$ matrices) are somewhat loose and rely on global min/max operations that can be sensitive to numerical scale differences across attention heads.
